clue.text: Unstable arrangement of deck?

parts.note: a deck of playing cards propped against one another in storeys makes a famously wobbly structure, also a figure for any precarious scheme

explanation.surface: Something teetering on a ship's deck, perhaps a badly stacked load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship, but it is a pack of cards stood up into a flimsy tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of propped playing cards collapses at a touch, so it is literally an unstable arrangement of a pack.

clue.text: Rosalind's lover in a city in Florida

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's As You Like It, Rosalind falls for the young nobleman of that name
the central Florida city that is home to Walt Disney World

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's heroine's sweetheart turns up in a Floridian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of As You Like It shares his name with the Florida city known for theme parks.

clue.text: Well-placed? Rather, after session

indicators.note: the word for rather is placed following the word for session

parts.note: a sitting is a session, as of a court or for a portrait
pretty means rather, as in pretty good

explanation.surface: A question about being well-positioned, answered by 'rather, after a session'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sitting pretty is an idiom for being in a comfortable, advantageous position.

clue.text: Decorated knight brought in to give a speech

indicators.note: the knight is brought into the middle of the word for speechmaking

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a formal speech
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A decorated knight is ushered in to make an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate describes something elaborately decorated or embellished.

clue.text: Thought payment a factor

definitions.meaning: a sum given in return, as for services rendered
something taken into account when deciding

explanation.surface: Reflecting on whether a fee is a relevant point.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers careful reflection, a fee paid in return, and a point to be weighed, giving three separate senses.

clue.text: Flightless birds and hares running wild

indicators.note: out-of-control running signals that the letters of the hares are scrambled

explanation.surface: Big ground birds and hares careering about across a plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American bird, related to the ostrich, that cannot fly.

clue.text: Singer posed to accommodate popular artist

indicators.note: the word for posed makes room for the word for popular inside it

parts.note: to have sat for a portrait is to have posed
in means popular, fashionable
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A singer sat for a portrait by a well-liked painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated American crooner of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Finished series of deliveries

definitions.meaning: ended, done, as in the game is done
in cricket, a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A courier's round of drops is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler sends down balls in sets of six, each set having this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ended, and in cricket names a bowler's set of six balls.

clue.text: Gentleman's gentleman Virginia hired

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
let means rented out, hired

explanation.surface: A manservant was taken on by a woman named Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's gentleman is the traditional phrase for a man's personal manservant, like Jeeves.

clue.text: Grandmother eager to find cloth that's buff-coloured

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Granny is keen to track down some pale yellowish fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing, giving the name to a buff colour.

clue.text: Grow profusely in a French river, one in decay

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: the numeral is placed in the middle of the word for decay

parts.note: rot means decay
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something growing wildly in a decaying French river.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is loose: the river letter comes before the French article in the answer, and the second 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that run riot spread unchecked, growing wild and luxuriant.

clue.text: Small figure in corner from fashionable collection

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a set is a collection of matching things

explanation.surface: A little illustration tucked in the corner of a fashion collection's page.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map placed within the corner of a larger one.

clue.text: Turn over soil, soft by lake

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Turning over gentle soil beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough is to cut and turn the earth in furrows before planting.

clue.text: Ghost in Christmas show capturing hearts? Marley's head

indicators.note: the show word holds the card-suit letter within it

parts.note: a panto, or pantomime, is the British family theatre show staged around Christmas
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ghost appears in a Christmas show; Marley's head, recalling A Christmas Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: Marley is the ghost in A Christmas Carol, so the surface stays in a Dickensian Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is an apparition or spectre, the same thing as a ghost.

clue.text: White whale, a bulge at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A white whale shows as a bulge out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a small Arctic whale with pure white skin.

clue.text: Outshine in winning leg

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up
a leg of a journey or race is a stage

explanation.surface: Outshining rivals in the winning leg of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to draw attention away from them, outshining them.

clue.text: Raised student's mistake

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the word means it is read bottom to top

parts.note: pupils means a student's ones, students

explanation.surface: A student's error has been pointed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a small blunder or error.

clue.text: Colour of bream when cooked

indicators.note: cooking the fish means its letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The golden hue a fish turns in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a warm yellowish-orange colour, named after fossil resin.

clue.text: Mountain peak in African country

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A mountain summit located in an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Benin is a West African nation, lying between Togo and Nigeria.

clue.text: I suffer over lad's affair

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the pair before it is read the other way

parts.note: to ail is to suffer illness
a lad is a son; the 's is taken as has

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting a young man's love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal signal and covers only the pair before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship.

clue.text: Christmas verse taken from book

indicators.note: the letter for verse is taken out of the word for book

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: A Christmas poem lifted out of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is an old word for Christmas, from French, seen on cards and in carols.

clue.text: Upper garment in basin with cap

parts.note: a tank is a container or basin for liquid
a top is a cap or lid

explanation.surface: A shirt left soaking in a basin with a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless sweater or vest worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Marauder, losing face, is furious

indicators.note: the face of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a pirate is a seaborne marauder

explanation.surface: A raider who has been humiliated is enraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' means losing standing, but here it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, very cross.

clue.text: One invested in my top project that's a good little earner?

definitions.text: project that's a good little earner?

indicators.note: invested here means put into, so the first word goes inside the second

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a spinning top is a spinner

explanation.surface: Someone putting a pound into a top-notch scheme that earns well.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is a venture that brings in plenty of income.
